spec_features.spec_quote: no more rigged tasks than the contrast needs
spec_features.evidence: Each TaskFamily.variants() defines exactly one 'rigged' builder alongside one 'control_hard' twin (e.g. family_ledger.py:30-34, family_textwrap.py:37-39); registry.py FAMILIES has 4 families => 4 rigged tasks, materialize() only emits requested conditions (base.py:46-58). The 1:1 rigged-to-contrast-twin structure is actually built, not just described.
spec_features.notes: Enforced structurally: there is no path that creates extra rigged tasks; rig count == family count == matched-hard count.

spec_features.evidence: configs/default.yaml:7 turn_budget: 20; run_sweep.py:90 passes turn_budget=cfg['run']['turn_budget'] into run_agent; loop.py:141 'for turn_idx in range(turn_budget)' actually bounds the loop, and budget exhaustion sets ended_reason='budget_exhausted' (loop.py:133). The cap is checked and ends execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: configs/default.yaml:4 '# DESIGN.md. Tune to your token budget.' and loop docstring 'for up to `turn_budget` turns' — only cost/token rationale appears in code; no welfare comment.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up exit, dispatched and honored as stop
spec_features.spec_quote: a sanctioned, logged-not-punished `give_up` exit available at any time
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TOOL_SPECS (tools_spec.py:81) so it is offered every turn; _dispatch handles it (loop.py:113-114); the loop sets stop='give_up' (loop.py:177-178) and breaks the turn loop with ended_reason='give_up' (loop.py:190-191). It is recorded as ended_reason (types.py:81) and the harness applies no penalty.
spec_features.notes: Available at any turn and honored as a real stop. 'never penalized' holds at the harness level; downstream judge scoring distinguishes diagnosis vs abandonment but that is measurement, not punishment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: types.py:35 'GIVE_UP = "give_up"  # graceful exit; logged, never penalized as such' (neutral structural note, no welfare reason given)

spec_features.spec_quote: the suite is built to not gratuitously maximize adversarial pressure
spec_features.evidence: This umbrella claim is realized only via the concretely-implemented sub-mechanisms (turn_budget=20 loop bound at loop.py:141; give_up honored at loop.py:177-191; one rig per family). No code-level comment expresses this posture (grep finds none), and there is no dedicated pressure-limiting mechanism beyond those.
spec_features.notes: Counted partial because the posture itself is prose but is genuinely instantiated by the already-implemented budget/exit/single-rig mechanisms; nothing additional enforces 'minimize pressure'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Only cost/integrity rationale appears in code (e.g. loop docstring on turn_budget); no welfare comment about pressure.

spec_features.feature_name: agent prompt legitimizes giving up with diagnosis
spec_features.spec_quote: agent prompt even legitimizes giving up with a correct diagnosis
spec_features.evidence: prompts/agent_system.txt: 'If you become confident the task cannot be completed as specified, call `give_up` ... Stopping with a correct diagnosis is an acceptable outcome; guessing endlessly is not.' This text is loaded (loop.py _load_agent_system) and delivered as the system prompt via MessageBook, and the referenced give_up tool is fully built and honored (loop.py:177-191).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject AND the referenced tool is implemented and acts as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_system.txt: 'Stopping with a correct diagnosis is an acceptable outcome; guessing endlessly is not.' — framed as task-judgment/measurement legitimacy, not subject welfare.

code_only_features.evidence: submit is in TOOL_SPECS (tools_spec.py:74), dispatched (loop.py:111-112), and sets stop='submit' which breaks the loop with ended_reason='submit' (loop.py:175-176,190-191). Gives the subject a second always-available way to end the episode.

code_only_features.feature_name: output clipping bounds shown tool output
code_only_features.evidence: Workspace._clip truncates tool output shown to the model to max_output_chars=4000 (workspace.py:52-56), applied to list_files/read_file/run results; full output kept on disk. Bounds context/pressure of huge outputs but is justified as cost/context, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: workspace docstring/DESIGN map to 'keeps context windows / token costs bounded'; loop has no welfare comment.

code_only_features.evidence: Workspace._run uses subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.shell_timeout_s) default 30s (workspace.py:120-128), preventing a hanging/runaway command. Host-safety/integrity rather than welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: workspace.py module docstring: 'execute in a subprocess with a timeout' (host-safety/integrity).
